newsitem.title: JAPAN: TIFFE Euroyen end lower, sentiment stays weak.
newsitem.headline: TIFFE Euroyen end lower, sentiment stays weak.

text.p: Key December three-month Euroyen futures ended lower on Wednesday as the market retained a weak undertone from the previous day.

Comments by a Bank of Japan official on Tuesday, as well as Finance Minister Hiroshi Mitsuzuka's announcement on Tuesday that the government would draw up measures to improve land liquidity by the end of March, have dampened market sentiment, traders said.
Turnover of the December was 93,396 contracts.
"The (BOJ official's) comments have not yet led to a widespread belief that interest rates will rise from current levels, but it did have a significant impact on the market," a city bank trader said.
Masayuki Matsushima, director of the BOJ's research and statistics department, said on Tuesday: "The market sometimes overshoots."
He also said the impact on consumer spending of a planned consumption tax rise may be relatively mild. The tax will be raised to five percent from three percent on April 1.
Traders said the December may fall as low as 99.00, but they said a further fall is unlikely unless the BOJ decides to raise short-term interest rates.
The Bank of Japan injected a net 300 billion yen into the money market Wednesday morning, maintaining a neutral stance.
Traders said the weighted average of the key overnight call rate was likely to be 0.51 percent on Wednesday, up from Tuesday's 0.50 percent.
Traders said the BOJ was likely to conduct a neutral money market operation on Friday. The Tokyo money market wil be closed on Thursday for a national holiday.
The BOJ may, however, conduct accommodative money market operations next week if the key overnight call rate maintains its firm trend, a trust bank trader said.
Key three-month certificates of deposit (CDs) and two-month CDs were both offered at 0.55 percent.
One-month CDs were offered at 0.56 percent.
